subject: DPA & TOMs: eSign flow, subprocessor onboarding & KMS approach
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeinc.com>, ACME Legal <legal@acmeinc.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: DPA/TOMs edits + KMS question (initial)

Hi Jane / ACME Legal team,

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Attached is our proposed TOMs exhibit (Redwood_TOMs_v3.pdf) and a first-pass redline of the DPA (DPA_Redlines_ACME.docx). A few items we want to surface explicitly so we can align before formal execution: 

- Subprocessors: please confirm the final list (we attached Subprocessor_List_ACME.xlsx with the current set). We understand you may want escalation rights for any new EU-region subprocessors.
- Key management: ACME asked about BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys. Our baseline is Redwood-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS and per-customer key separation; we can offer a BYOK option via AWS KMS cross-account grant for an enterprise add-on.
- Encryption and access controls: TOMs v3 includes role-based access, quarterly key rotation, and audit logging — we flagged the sections we expect you to review.
- Execution: once we have agreement on the few open points below we can e-sign via DocuSign.

Action items / asks from ACME:
1) Please send the requested DPA redlines inline (we prefer Word for tracking).
2) Confirm whether you require BYOK for production or whether a Redwood-managed, segregated-key approach with attestable audit logs is acceptable.
3) Provide SOC2 type II report or link; if unavailable, indicate timing.

I've looped Kar (cc) for pricing and monica for onboarding sequencing. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps — propose Tue morning.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_TOMs_v3.pdf (TOMs exhibit, 9 pages), DPA_Redlines_ACME.docx (initial redline), Subprocessor_List_ACME.xlsx (current list)

From: ACME Legal <legal@acmeinc.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeinc.com>, Tim Lawrence <tim.lawrence@acmeinc.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA/TOMs edits + KMS question (ACME comments)

Maya — thanks for the materials. We reviewed with our security team and attached our annotated redline (DPA_Redlines_ACME_annotated.docx). High-level items: 

- Subprocessors: we require 30 days’ notice for any new subprocessors with the right to opt out for EU data. Please confirm you can provide a single point of contact for subprocessor notifications.
- KMS / Key custody: preference is customer-controlled keys (BYOK) for production workloads. If Redwood cannot support BYOK immediately, we need written controls showing segregated keys, HSM protection, and audited key-access events.
- Key escrow/import: if BYOK is supported via KMS imports, we need a documented technical walk-through and an assurance that Redwood will not retain plaintext or import materials into our account without explicit permission.
- Data transfers: for EU→US processing, we need the standard transfer mechanism (SCCs) and assurances around onward transfers to subprocessors.
- Evidence: please attach SOC2 report or cert portal link and your latest penetration test summary.

On execution timing: we prefer DocuSign for speed. We ask that both the DPA and TOMs exhibit be included in the same envelope. Please let us know who will be the Redwood signer.

Regards,
ACME Legal

Attachments: DPA_Redlines_ACME_annotated.docx (ACME comments)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA/TOMs edits + KMS question — recommended negotiation stance

Team — quick internal note after reviewing ACME's annotated redline and security asks. Proposed position:

- Subprocessors: Accept 30-day notice, provide POC; add a clause for emergency patching that permits immediate onboarding with retrospective notice for critical security subprocessors.
- KMS: Offer a two-path approach:
  1) Redwood-managed HSM-backed keys (default) with per-customer key isolation, detailed audit logs, and quarterly key rotation; OR
  2) BYOK (enterprise add-on): support AWS KMS cross-account grants + instructions for key policy and IAM role to allow envelope encryption (recommended pilot).
- Key escrow: We will not hold ACME plaintext keys. For KMS import workflows, provide a step-by-step guide and require ACME to provision the key in their account and grant the minimal cross-account decrypt/encrypt role.
- SCCs & transfers: Confirm SCCs included; legal should add a clause on onward transfer obligations for subprocessors.

Risks / effort: BYOK pilot requires infra work (estimated 3–4 sprints) and a runbook for onboarding. Recommend we offer BYOK as a time-boxed pilot (30–60 days) and accept Redwood-managed keys for go-live if ACME needs faster execution.

Next steps: Maya — propose we send a consolidated DPA/TOMs redline that: (a) accepts the 30-day notice with emergency carveout, (b) includes the two-path KMS appendix, and (c) attaches SOC2 link and pen-test summary. Legal (me/Monica) to review final language prior to DocuSign.

-Kar
VP, Legal Ops (internal)

Attachment: KMS_implementation_notes.pdf (internal tech summary)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
To: ACME Legal <legal@acmeinc.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeinc.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Updated DPA + TOMs (consolidated redline) — ready for eSign

Jane / ACME team — thanks for the annotated comments. Attached is our consolidated redline (DPA_Redlines_ACME.docx) which: 

- Accepts 30-day subprocessor notice plus emergency-onboarding carveout.
- Adds a Key Management appendix with two supported deployment options: Redwood-managed HSM keys (default) OR BYOK via AWS KMS cross-account grant (enterprise add-on).
- Confirms SCCs will be attached for EU transfers and that Redwood requires subprocessors to follow the same transfer constraints.

We also attached our SOC2 Type II artifact link in the TOMs exhibit and a short pen-test summary.

If this looks good, we will include both the DPA and the TOMs exhibit in one DocuSign envelope for signature. Please confirm the ACME signer (name & title) and whether you want Redwood to initiate the envelope.

DocuSign envelope (draft): https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC12345DEF
Attachments included in envelope: DPA_Redlines_ACME.docx, Redwood_TOMs_v3.pdf

Requested next steps from ACME:
- Confirm acceptance of either: Redwood-managed keys (with audit attestation) OR BYOK pilot (we will provide onboarding guide).
- Provide signer details for envelope.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-minute review call if you'd like.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Redlines_ACME.docx (consolidated), Redwood_TOMs_v3.pdf, SOC2_Link.txt (link to cert portal)

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

Regards,
ACME Legal
